title: Plural personal pronouns
summary: Learn the subject pronouns for groups and plural address.
objectives: Match me, te, and he to their meanings.
Separate the group speaking from the group addressed.
Use he for people being discussed.

sections.title: Three group pronouns
paragraphs: Me means “we”: the speaker belongs to the group. Te means plural “you”: two or more people are addressed.
He means “they” when a group of people is discussed.

sections.title: Follow the viewpoint
paragraphs: Ask who is speaking, who is listening, and who is being discussed. That viewpoint tells you which pronoun to choose.
These short pronouns have no ending in the subject form taught here.

steps: The speaker is inside the group.
The people are discussed, not addressed.

commonMistakes: Do not confuse the speaker group me with the listener group te.
Use he for people, not as the direct form for “you”.
Keep each pronoun as one separate word.
